newsitem.title: FRANCE: ONIC head says higher malt refund seems justified.
newsitem.headline: ONIC head says higher malt refund seems justified.

text.p: The head of France's grain authority on Wednesday backed malt exporters who are trying to get European Union export refunds raised by the European Commission.
ONIC director general Alain Moulinier said maltsters wanted monthly fixing of malt refunds using a standard coefficient tied to barley refunds and this seemed fair.
"This seems a justified request to me, but at this stage it is not being followed up by the EU," Moulinier told a regular monthly news conference.
Malt firms want the Commission to raise the current malt export refund because the most widely accepted coefficient -- 1.3 times the barley refund -- points to an increase.
The firms have mostly refused to draw current EU malt export licences, prompting suggestions that the EU might try to jog them along by threatening to claw back all or part of any future increase.
Britain and Belgium support the maltsters' demands.

The EU has given no indication whether it will raise the refund at weekly grain talks on Thursday. But one EU cereals management committee source said last week that the Commission did not at that stage believe an increase was justified.
Traders say the latest barley export refund of 30.98 Ecus per tonne implies a malt refund of just over 40 Ecus per tonne if EU definitions are applied strictly.
But opponents of an increase say malting premiums are wider on the world market than in Europe at the moment, and the current malt export refund of 32.5 Ecus per tonne is enough.
British maltsters said on Tuesday they were hoping for an increase in the refund this week, now that there was a clearer picture of barley availabilities around the world.
